current: The direct path exists in its permitted (paper) form and the requirement's chaos check is now demonstrated on the pieces the binary is assembled from. qip_edge::cell::Cell::work sends orders straight to the node's in-process SimulatedGateway and fills come back through the same gateway; the Requoter's cancel and replacement go the same way. The new test takes the journal store away (a KeyValueStore that fails every call) and points the mesh link at a dead centre, then runs three turns in the order serve() in main.rs runs them -- Cell::flush, MeshLink::exchange, run_pass -- asserting on each turn that both outages are real: an order is sent and rests at the venue, a stale order is cancelled and replaced, a fill is booked under the cell's own id and agrees with the venue's ledger, and the cell is not halted. When the store returns one flush ships the whole backlog and the store's batches verify as one chain from the session's start. In the deployed loop, however, serve() still runs the blocking flush and the blocking centre exchange on the same thread immediately before each pass: a failure of either is reported and the pass runs, but a store or centre that is slow rather than dead delays the pass by up to its I/O timeout.

gap: One thing remains, and it is the coupling rather than the check. The deployed serve loop serialises a blocking journal flush and a blocking centre exchange ahead of every pass on the pass's own thread. Neither sits between the order and the venue, and an unreachable store or centre fails fast and the pass runs -- that is now proven -- but a slow one delays the pass by up to its I/O timeout, which is the synchronous dependency the requirement's rationale warns against, and no test bounds it. serve() itself is a function of a binary and is driven by no test; the chaos test replays its three calls in its order. The only venue is the in-process simulator, so the gateway leg is a function call, and the journal sink is the node's StoreMirror: the event-fabric outbox in qip_edge_node::event_fabric is not called from main.rs.
